messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT  Multi-region traffic shift + TLS/edge anomalies detected. GSLB moved traffic from eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 at 2036-01-18T05:08:20Z after eu-west healthchecks degraded. Symptoms: elevated 5xx and 525/526 TLS handshake errors at the edge for some clients, mixed resolver answers, and token validation races. Paging on-call: @vikram.shah.

vikram.shah: on-call, looking now. seeing a spike in edge TLS failures (525) and backend 5xx in eu-west. what's the regional breakdown? (grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/edge-tls)

zoe.kim: eu-west origin LBs reported intermittent cert validation errors after a maintenance cert-rotation job completed at 05:03Z. Some origin nodes got the new cert bundle, others still had the old chain, causing TLS rehandshakes to fail for connections proxied by CDN endpoints. That likely explains 525/526 at the edge.

peter.lopez: additionally GSLB weight reduction happened but many CDNs and ISP caches keep sending traffic to eu-west IPs. long-lived HTTP/2 sessions from mobile clients are still pinned by CDNs which multiplex to eu-west origin, so DNS change didn't fully evacuate traffic. logs show many reused h2 connections. sample edge lines:

```
Jan 18 05:06:54 edge-07 proxy: client=203.0.113.150:51222 reused-h2 conn=3 backend=eu-lb-02 tls_err=525
```

vikram.shah: immediate plan: 1) request provider withdraw for eu-west anycast (if anycast persisted) and force GSLB weight 0, 2) apply emergency TLS rollback on eu-west origin to restore uniform cert chain, 3) initiate conntrack flush and aggressive http2 session purge, 4) enable short token-rebind endpoint to revalidate sessions to target region, 5) customer comms. Starting with weight 0 now.

deploy-bot: Executing gslbctl set-weight --record api.redwood.ai --region eu-west-1 --weight 0 --reason "emergency zero due to mixed cert rotation". Change accepted (chg-id: G-2102).

nina.gupta: cert-rotation job logs show a race where the signing CA bundle rotated in two phases; a subset of instances pulled new bundle and restarted the origin process, others remained with pre-rotation cert until their config sync kicked in. I'll trigger a coordinated rollback to the previous cert across the eu fleet.

zoe.kim: while rollback runs, pushing edge policy to return 503+Retry-After for write endpoints when backend=eu-west and pool_state=draining to nudge clients to re-resolve. Also pushing an http2 session purge on edge nodes.

```
# edge commands
edgectl set-policy --name emergency_http2_purge --match ":host=api.redwood.ai" --action "purge-h2-sessions; return 503; header Retry-After:4"
```

zoe.kim: initiated purge. active h2 reused conns dropped from ~2400 -> ~180 within 90s.

peter.lopez: implemented conntrack flush on eu-west NAT nodes and set LB pool to draining: 

```
redwood-lbctl set-pool-state --region eu-west-1 --pool-id pool-api-33 --state draining --force-timeout 30s
for n in $(redwood-nodes list --region eu-west-1 --role nat); do ssh $n 'sudo conntrack -D --orig-port-dst 443 || true'; done
```

deploy-bot: Cert rollback started: origin-cert-manager rollback --region eu-west-1 --to-tag cert-2025-12-31a. Canary rollout to 20% of origin nodes -> 100%. Status: 55% at 05:10Z.

support-bot: initial customer impact: ~22 reports in last 8m, mostly mobile app sessions failing with token-exp and TLS errors. 5 enterprise customers flagged (authstream and bulk ingest failures). posting initial status to status.redwood.ai.

nina.gupta: rollback completed at 05:11:38Z on eu-west origin fleet. Verified uniform cert chain present across all origin nodes.

peter.lopez: after rollback and conntrack purge we see TLS 525/526 errors drop sharply at the edge. GSLB change INSYNC internally, but some ISPs still return eu-west IPs. sample dig variance: 

```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
18.205.44.11

$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @9.9.9.9
52.12.34.11
```

vikram.shah: token validation errors persist for a subset: reports show tokens with issuer bound to eu-west key being validated in us-east after failover -> kid mismatches. we'll enable a temporary token-rebind endpoint (POST /internal/token/rebind) that will accept an existing token and reissue a region-agnostic token after a quick revalidation. This reduces invalid-token surface while we monitor. Security has been consulted.

nina.gupta: token-rebind hotpatch prepared. deploy-bot will roll to edge and auth services canary 5% -> 50% -> 100%.

deploy-bot: Hotfix deploy started: auth-service v2026-01-17b (token-rebind) and edge-verifier v2026-01-17b. Canary 5% -> 50% at 05:13Z.

support-bot: customers reporting token errors dropping after token-rebind reach ~20% canary. enterprise customer B confirms partial resume of scheduled job after rebind.

vikram.shah: monitoring: 5xx dropping from 7.9% -> 1.7% after combined rollback + purge + token rebind. p95 latency for affected clients improving. keep region at weight 0 for 20m.

peter.lopez: infra follow-ups: ensure cert-rotation job uses a coordinated rollout lock and healthcheck that verifies TLS chain across all origin nodes before marking job success. Creating INFRA-5201. Also add automated HTTP/2 session purge when pool enters draining state (INFRA-5202).

nina.gupta: security note: token-rebind adds slight increased token reissue volume; will scope rate limits and audit logs. Create SEC-2003 to review long-term region-agnostic token model.

support-bot: customer-impact summary: 22 reports, 5 enterprise escalations, no data loss. Updates posted at 05:14Z and 05:20Z. enterprise outreach in progress.

vikram.shah: checklist to close emergency phase: 
- cert rollback verified across eu-west (nina)
- LB drain + conntrack purge complete (peter)
- token-rebind stable and auth-errors baseline (nina/support)
- customer notifications and enterprise follow-up (support-bot)

peter.lopez: LB drain completed at 05:14:20Z. conntrack flush confirmed. active flows to eu-west < 5.

nina.gupta: token-rebind rollout at 100% by 05:15:12Z. auth mismatch events reduced to baseline <0.2%.

support-bot: posted customer final update at 05:16Z. enterprise follow-ups scheduled.

vikram.shah: incident declared RESOLVED for availability at 05:17:00Z (service availability restored, TLS and auth errors at baseline). handing postmortem to @nina.gupta. Great work team. :tada:

incident-bot: Incident record saved: incident-2036-01-18-eu-cert-rotation-drift. Postmortem owner: nina.gupta. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/incident/2102468100

nina.gupta: will publish postmortem with timeline, root cause, and action owners by EOD. initial actions: INFRA-5201 (coordinated cert-rotation lock), INFRA-5202 (auto http2 purge on drain), SEC-2003 (token model review), DEVX-3210 (staging test for resolver caching + http2 reuse).

vikram.shah: handing off monitoring to nina for 1h. if anything else crops up ping me. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
